daily.note: I need these pine logs for the new beams going up on the lane. Good wood makes a home that stands through every storm.
Planks first, then the walls. Smooth, sweet-smelling pine is the best start for any cozy cottage I know.
Shingles keep the rain off sleeping pets. Lay pine planks underneath, and the roof will shed weather for years to come.
Strong strings keep my looms together through the long evenings. They remind me of the sanctuary weavers, who clothed monsters and people alike.
Soft plant fiber is the heart of a warm blanket. Bring me a sackful and I will weave something cozy for your pets.
My pies need plump berries by the basketful, the sweeter the better. Berries were a treat at old sanctuary feasts too, so let's keep that going.
A little jar of berry compote is perfect on a cold morning. Three or eight jars, and the bakery shelves will look lovely again.
Hungry travelers always ask for minnow stew with toasted hazelnuts on the side. Serve it warm and nobody leaves grumbling.
Copper bars are what I need to shape proper tools. Bring them over and I'll hammer out something worth keeping.
Good copper ore makes a good bar, and a good bar makes a good day at the forge. Keep the ore coming, friend.
Rabbit meat feeds a whole table and keeps the hearth warm. I'll share what I can, and the rest goes to the village kitchens.
The old sanctuary well is said to glow under a full moon, and the minnows there are always lively. Bring a bucketful and we'll both be happy.
Meadow herbs grew in the old sanctuary gardens, where pets and people once shared the terraces. Gather some for the healing hut, please.
A vigor tonic gives tired pets a little spring in their step. I'm running low, so three or six bottles would help a lot.
Rabbit roast was always served at the sanctuary feast hall, a dish for the whole gathering. Bring a few and I'll keep the tables full.
The village needs stone for paths and walls, and the mill needs it too. Please gather what you can, and thank you for helping our little town grow.
Oak logs are hard to come by, but they're worth every splinter. A proper hall needs proper timber, and this is it.
Oak planks are the backbone of anything built to last. Smooth them well, and they'll look good for generations.
Old frames like these held up the sanctuary feast hall, where people and pets once dined together. Two or five would be a fine start.
Iron bars are the stuff of strong tools and stronger gates. Bring what you can spare, and I'll make it sing on the anvil.
Iron nails hold a roof through the wildest storm. I need plenty, so keep the hammer swinging and the nails coming.
Honeyed hazelnuts are a treat the whole village loves, and my little ones can't get enough. Sweet, crunchy, and worth the walk.
A grilled trout dish brings the regulars back every night. Bring me a few and I'll put them on the best plates in town.
Glowcap tonic is for the bravest sleepers and the weariest pets. I'm short on it, so three or five bottles would mean a lot.
Mushrooms and honeycomb make a fine tonic base, and I have a lovely recipe to try. Gather them carefully, dear, and bring them along.
Brook trout is the sweetest catch in the stream, and the pets go wild for it. Fifteen or thirty would keep my kitchen busy.
Venison makes a proper supper for a hungry hunter's family. Bring me a good stock and I'll see it reaches every kitchen in town.
Deer hides and sinew make the warmest mittens and the strongest straps. Bring them to my loom and I'll stitch you something fine.
The village foundry needs iron ore to keep the forge hot through the cold season. Your help keeps our little town running smoothly.
Cedar logs smell like a forest after rain, and they make the finest beams. I'm starting a new hall and need every good log I can get.
Cedar planks are lighter and kinder to work with than oak. Bring them along and we'll raise something beautiful together.
Cedar shingles shed the rain beautifully and last for years. They'll make the roof of the new hall look like a storybook.
Steel bars are for the finest tools in the valley. I'll be working late on these, so bring them whenever you can spare.
Coal keeps the forge burning hot enough to shape steel. Give me a good heap and I'll have the village tools ready in no time.
Boar meat is rich, dark, and filling, the kind that keeps a hunter going all day. Bring a good haul, and some bone for broth too.
Rock bass hide in the deep pools, but they make a hearty supper for anyone brave enough to catch them. Fifteen or thirty would fill my crates.
Mountain sage grows only in the high meadows, and its scent calms even the wildest pets. Bring a good bunch and I'll brew well.
Rock bass chowder is my pride, warm and thick with cream. Bring me the fish and the rest of the pot will come together nicely.
A bone broth tonic warms the bones and steadies the heart. Three or five jars would keep my winter patients snug and happy.
The old heart-shaped shrine by the sanctuary once held gems like these. Please bring what you find, and we'll polish them with care.
Willow logs bend beautifully and make the loveliest curved rafters. I'd be grateful for a bundle, dear.
Willow planks are soft, pale, and pretty, just right for a homey kitchen. Bring a stack and I'll get to work right away.
Mythril is the rarest metal I've ever worked, and it rings like a bell. A few bars would make a tool worth passing down.
Bog lilies bloom beside the old moonlit well, where pets once came to drink. Bring fifteen or thirty and I'll share them with everyone.
Marsh eels are slippery customers, but they make the tastiest skewers in the region. Bring them along and I'll pay you fairly.
Fowl meat and feathers are my bread and butter in the reed beds. Bring a good haul, and I'll see the feathers become pillows.
Candied lily nuts are my newest treat, sweet and a little bit magical. Three or six would make a lovely gift for the mayor's table.
Eel skewers are the talk of the inn this season. Bring me the eels and I'll grill them up for the evening crowd.
Marsh tonic keeps the swampfolk healthy through the damp months. Three or five bottles would go a long way in the healing hut.
Willow shingles are light, strong, and shed rain like a dream. Bring them along and we'll finish the roof before the weather turns.
Ashwood is the heartwood of the mountains, dark and strong as iron. I'd be honored to start a beam with a bundle of these.
Ashwood planks carry a faint warm glow, and they're a joy to work. A stack of them would make the finest workshop in the valley.
Emberite bars hold heat like nothing else I've forged. I need a few to finish the shrine work, and I'm grateful for your help.
Fire blooms glow like tiny lanterns at dusk, and they make a fierce, bright tonic. Bring fifteen or thirty and the healing hut will be cheerful.
Lava crabs are tough and fiery, but the broth they make is the best in the caldera. Bring a dozen or two, and I'll be most grateful.
Ram meat is hearty mountain fare, perfect for a long winter's feast. Bring the meat and horns, and I'll share a good portion with the village.
Lava crab boil is the feast we serve when the whole village gathers. Bring the crabs and I'll have the cauldron bubbling by dusk.
Ember tonic is warm and bright, a comfort for pets who've worked hard all week. Three or five bottles would be a real gift to my patients.
A ram roast is the centerpiece of any proper celebration. Bring me the meat and I'll bake it golden, the way my grandmother did.
The town's forge needs emberite ore to keep the hearth going through the coming season. Thank you for every stone you carry.
Ember resin is a warm, sweet glue, and ashwood is its perfect partner. Bring them to my loom and I'll weave something lovely.

great.note: The old mill needs a full repair before the harvest festival. Planks, nails, and shingles from every corner of the village will bring it back to life.
Harvest Festival is coming, and I want a feast for the whole village. Compote, stew, and roast will bring everyone to the square together.
The festival needs new tools and fittings, and I can't manage it alone. Bring copper bars, fittings, and nails, and we'll make it a proud day.
Every year the weavers ask for fresh strings and hides for the festival banners. Let's make this the finest year yet.
The old hall roof has seen better days, and the village deserves a new one. Oak planks, shingles, and frames will keep us dry for years.
The inn is hosting a banquet for travelers from far away. Trout, hazelnuts, and stew will make them feel right at home.
The ironworks needs a big order to keep the bellows going. Iron bars and nails, and I'll have the valley's gates ready in no time.
My shelves are nearly bare, and winter is coming. Glowcap tonic, whisper brew, and mushrooms would keep the whole village healthy.
We're raising a cedar hall for village meetings, much like the sanctuary feast hall of old. Planks, shingles, and frames will make it sing.
The hillside supper is the biggest night of the year at my inn. Chowder, broth, and boar meat will feed every hungry soul in town.
The steelworks needs a big batch of steel and coal before the snow falls. Bring what you can, and we'll forge something to remember.
The gem cutters are opening a new shop in the square, and they need a fine stock. Rough gems, tusks, and elixirs will make it shine.
We're mending the old willow bridge over the brook, the one monsters and people once crossed together. Planks and shingles will keep it strong.
The mistfen feast is a night to remember, with pies, skewers, and candied nuts. Bring me the goods and we'll make the mists proud.
I've been asked to forge a mythril piece for the town's old gate, a gift of rare silver. Bars and rivets, and I'll do it right.
The marsh folk are sick, and their remedies are running low. Tonics, lilies, and feathers would bring them comfort through the damp season.
The village wants a grand ashwood gate for the old sanctuary grounds, one built to last for ages. Planks and logs, and I'll carve the rest.
The caldera feast brings the whole valley to one table, fiery and warm. Crab boil, roast, and pudding, and a welcome for every guest.
The big forge needs emberite and coal to burn hot enough for the great bell. Bring me the bars and fuel, and let's make it ring.
The healing hut is running low on warm remedies for the cold nights ahead. Tonics, fire blooms, and horns would see us through the season.
